criteria.criterion: A local path or file:// origin produces no remote field (absent, not null) and nothing in the repo identity names the path.
criteria.evidence: export.go publicRemote returns false for file:// and path forms; repoIdentity then falls back to the directory name; Remote has omitempty; test cases 1-2 assert absence

criteria.criterion: An https origin with user info, a query and a fragment is exported as https://<host>/<path> only, e.g. https://example.com/org/r.git; no token, user or fragment survives anywhere in the repo identity, including its name.
criteria.evidence: publicRemote cuts at ?/#, strips user info; the name is derived from the cleaned URL; the test asserts remote, name 'r', and absence of tok123/alice/frag in the marshalled repo

criteria.criterion: An ssh:// URL loses its user info; an scp-like origin keeps its host and path.
criteria.evidence: test cases ssh://bob@git.example.com:2222/org/r.git -> ssh://git.example.com:2222/org/r.git and git@github.com:org/r.git -> github.com:org/r.git

criteria.criterion: Every exported record still validates as export/v1.
criteria.evidence: schemas/export.v1.json updated in step (remote not required, string); the gate validates each record

criteria.criterion: internal/cli/export_test.go holds TestExportRemoteForms covering a temp-path origin and an https origin with user info and a query; it fails against the base.
criteria.evidence: export_test.go:167 TestExportRemoteForms; the base exported the local path and the token query, so the temp-path and https cases would fail

notes: The test's bad-substring loop has a redundant 'bad != filepath.Base(dir)' clause; harmless.
